counterfactual_missing_items: No bone marrow biopsy result is provided to confirm aplastic anemia
No raw span directly names aplastic anemia
No cytogenetic or MDS workup is reported
decisive_items: pancytopenia: platelet count 85×10^9/L, white-cell count 2.3×10^9/L (neutrophils 1.3×10^9/L, monocytes 0.2×10^9/L), and hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL
Skin biopsy showed dermal neutrophils with upper dermal edema and a subepidermal blister, consistent with bullous Sweet’s syndrome
Her blood counts remained low: hemoglobin 13.0 g/dL, white-cell count 1.7×10^9/L (neutrophils 0.5×10^9/L, monocytes 0.1×10^9/L), and platelets 49×10^9/L
response.rationale: R1 best explains the full picture: pancytopenia, persistent low counts, and Sweet’s syndrome as an associated hematologic phenomenon. R6 is only a presumptive label and is disconfirmed by lack of response to steroids/IVIG and by the full pancytopenia; R4 is a restatement of the blood count; R5 is a skin manifestation; R2 is excluded by negative ANA.

rejected.why: Only family history; ANA negative and no lupus features.
Pancytopenia is a lab finding, not a diagnosis; same raw span as R1.
Bullous Sweet’s syndrome is a dermatologic manifestation, not the underlying cause of pancytopenia.
